trickyParts: A clean merge is not a safe merge here. Three of the four merge defects of this round were invisible to go build and go vet and were caught only by a test: a queued write that a later read in the same transaction depends on, an artifacts row a read needs that the branch only queues, and a fixture holding a row where the branch now holds an owner lock. Anyone merging main into this branch again should run the api, docs, refs and pmdoc suites at the merge head, not just build it.

requestArtifactApproval's second attachApproval could not survive the write phase, since the rows it read are queued. approvalAfterRequest applies waitingOnExpression's rule in memory over the approval read before the writes. It is correct only because this route writes nothing else that read touches and holds the owner lock until it commits; a later change to what a request writes must revisit it.

The xid-window rig's D6 timing rule did not catch the unjoined approval-request route: its post-write reads are fast queries back to back on this fixture. The two new approval tests use the file's other shape instead, refusing any statement in the window beside the write batch and its COMMIT.

This pod cannot report a green docs or api package reliably: its legion_test role is neither a superuser nor a member of pg_signal_backend, so storetest's `drop database … with (force)` cannot terminate a test database's autovacuum worker and the package exits FAIL after every test has passed. Judge such a run by its --- FAIL lines, not its package line.

Two tests fail only under a parallel full suite on this 2-CPU pod and pass alone: TestEveryRouteAnswersAStoredTreeOutsideTheSchemaAlike (10.00 s against 8.47 s alone) and TestReplyToNestedCommentUsesThreadRoot (10 of 10 alone).
deviations: The 18 conflicted files of the first forward merge were resolved by six deep-worker subagents working on disjoint files at the same time rather than one at a time. The rule's reason is that a check one worker runs sees another's half-made edits; here no worker could run a check at all, because the module does not compile until every marker is gone, so each was told to run none. Every group was verified afterwards by one build, vet and suite run of mine.

GitHub ran no check on this branch between d3218a11 and 6e8e3c79: it computes no merge ref for a conflicting head. The three merges were the only way back to a readable CI, and the first two heads carry no CI result of their own.
discoveredComplexity: main moved three times during this round (f8f0425b, 0642a37a, 99565624, and 079e70fe in between), and GitHub reported the branch CONFLICTING after the first two. A branch of this size against this repository's merge rate needs its forward merge and its round of fixes in one push, which is what this round does.
